output.methodChoice: No catalogue items collected. I compared floors 6-8 with floors 1-5 and checked the floors 6-8 scores by checkout date against the outage dates. The initial evidence already separates the candidate causes, and no catalogue item looked likely to change an answer.
output.brief:
Dana — the August dip is a cooling failure, not Orrin or the kiosks.

Chiller CH-2, which cools floors 6–8, failed on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August because the part wasn't in stock. Guests on those floors scored us 6.8 during that stretch, against 8.5 before and about 8.5 after the repair. Floors 1–5 stayed near 8.5 all month. Heat is 56 of 74 negative comments and all of the rise in desk complaints.

Cleanliness scores, independent inspection pass rates, kiosk use, queue times and check-in scores are flat, and the survey method didn't change. So don't serve notice on Orrin, don't pull the kiosks, and don't drop floors 6–8 from the reported score; explain it instead.

The 6% rate rise is unresolved: value scores dip every August and the data can't separate the two. Leave rates alone and watch September value scores.

Next: reschedule the overdue maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spares on site, and write an outage guest-recovery procedure. Apologies and credits already went to affected guests.

I'm very sure about the cooling cause, less sure about rates.
